title: Add burst usage report export (scheduled + on-demand) for CS and customers
author: Chloe Martin
description: Context: As we move Dedicated burst capacity through beta → GA, CS and customers need a consistent, auditable report they can pull (or receive on a schedule) that answers: (1) how much burst they used, (2) when they hit peaks, and (3) why they were denied. This PR adds a small reporting pipeline in the control plane that generates per-tenant burst usage exports (CSV + JSON), stores them in our reporting bucket, and exposes them via an RBAC-protected API used by Console + internal CS tooling. The report is time-windowed (daily by default; weekly optional), includes region/hardware segmentation, and aggregates by denial reason code. Key outputs: burst GPU-seconds and tokens (from metering), peak burst ratio vs baseline (from tenant config + runtime usage), denial counts/rates by reason (e.g., FLEET_SAFETY_CAP, TENANT_BURST_CAP, COOLDOWN_ACTIVE, POOL_SATURATED, TELEMETRY_LAG_GUARD), and top peak windows (15m buckets). Scheduling: a new scheduled job runs at 00:20 UTC daily; backfill endpoint supports on-demand export for a given window (guarded). Storage: reports are written to s3://redwood-reporting-prod/burst-usage/v1/{tenant_id}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/... with server-side encryption and a 90-day retention lifecycle rule (configurable). Access: GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/reports/burst-usage?start=...&end=... returns metadata + a short-lived signed URL; Console shows "Download report" and internal CS tool can fetch via the same endpoint. Security/compliance: adds audit events for report generation and download, and ensures tenant_id scoping + support read-only role gating. Observability: emits report generation duration, failures, and export size metrics; adds a dashboard panel link in the runbook. Notes: This intentionally does not introduce email delivery in v1 (CS asked for it; we can add later once we align on templates + unsubscribe policy).
commits: control-plane: add BurstUsageReportGenerator and v1 export schema
reporting: add scheduled job + backfill CLI for burst usage reports
api: add tenant report endpoints + signed URL plumbing
audit: add events for report.generated + report.downloaded
metrics: export report generation metrics + failure reasons
tests: golden tests for CSV/JSON + RBAC coverage
docs: internal README for CS usage + troubleshooting
changed_areas: Control plane reporting subsystem (new burst usage generator + storage writer)
Tenant Reports API (new endpoints + RBAC checks)
Billing/metering integration (consume burst usage aggregates; idempotent window reads)
api_changes: GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/reports/burst-usage (list report artifacts for a time window; returns signed download URLs)
report_fields_v1: denied_by_reason (flattened columns in CSV; map in JSON)
operational_notes: Job runs daily at 00:20 UTC; retries with exponential backoff; hard timeout 10m per tenant/window.
If metering aggregates are delayed > 30m, report is generated with partial_data=true and a warning in notes; next day's report will include fully reconciled numbers.
Signed URLs expire after 15 minutes; report listing endpoint returns only the metadata for authorized callers.
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Please confirm we aren’t exploding label cardinality with tenant_id for the new metrics.
Chloe Martin (author): Metrics are emitted with tenant_tier + region + hw_class only. tenant_id is only present in logs (hashed) and in the report artifacts themselves.
Cole Summers: How are we reconciling metering delays? CS will get angry if daily exports don’t match invoices.

Chloe Martin (author): Added partial_data flag + notes when aggregates are behind; export job uses the same reconciliation window as billing (T+24h) by default, and on-demand export requires specifying start/end explicitly.
Sean Gallagher: Please add an alert for repeated export job failures; otherwise CS will find out via a customer escalation.
Chloe Martin (author): Added burst_report_export_failures_total alert (5 failures / 30m) and linked runbook section with remediation steps.
Rachel Kim: Can Support download reports for a tenant without full admin privileges?
Chloe Martin (author): Yes—new RBAC capability 'tenant.reports.read' is included in SupportReadOnly; export/backfill remains Admin/CSOps only.
Miguel Santos: Request: include denial reason breakdown because customers ask "why 429" constantly.
Chloe Martin (author): Included denied_by_reason with the standard reason codes from pr-23795; CSV includes one column per reason for easy pivoting.
qa_notes: Validated daily schedule in staging with 3 tenants across us-east H100 + eu-west L40S; reports created and downloadable via signed URL.
Golden tests verify stable column ordering in CSV and schema_v1 versioning in JSON.
Manual RBAC checks: SupportReadOnly can list/download; cannot trigger export. TenantAdmin can list/download only for their own tenant.
rollout_plan: Deploy behind feature flag: burst_reports_enabled (default off).
Enable in staging for internal tenants, then enable for beta tenants in us-east H100 only.
After 72h with no job failure alerts and acceptable report generation latency, expand allowlist to eu-west L40S.
GA: enable globally for all burst-enabled Dedicated tenants; keep export endpoint rate-limited.
merge_outcome: Merged to main; scheduled job disabled by default until rollout gates are flipped.
release_notes: Dedicated burst: Added downloadable burst usage reports (daily/weekly) including peak usage and denial reason breakdowns for customers and CS.
